newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL internet users touch 40,000.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL internet users touch 40,000.

text.p: India's monopoly state-run international telecommunications provider, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) said on Wednesday that it had more than 40,000 internet subscribers.

"The total number of internet subscribers on our system has crossed 40,000 and the average growth per month is 10 to 12 percent," B.K. Syngal, VSNL's chairman and managing director, told Reuters in an interview.
He expected the number to cross 100,000 by the end of this year, as VSNL was adding between 4,000 and 5,000 subscribers a month.
VSNL is the only commercial internet service provider in India. It started internet services on August 15, 1995.

The company's monopoly is expected to end soon, the communications ministry had said recently, stating that it would announce an internet policy after the next meeting of the Telecommunications Comission.

Apart from VSNL, there is only one other body, the Department of Electronics, that provides internet access. Its service is called the Education and Research Network (ERNET) and access is only granted to institutional and non-profit organisations.
Market sources estimate that ERNET had between 40,000 and 60,000 subscribers.
